https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text: Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog. US president Donald Trump said he ordered the Pentagon to scale back “inappropriate and hostile” military drills with South Korea, hours before the exercises began on Monday. The drills under Ulchi Freedom Shield, one of two major annual exercises held by South Korea and the US, start on Monday and run until 27 August. They were expected to involve about 18,000 South Korean troops, alongside US forces and personnel from 11 of the 18 member states of the United Nations Command (UNC), the multinational body that oversees the 1953 armistice that halted hostilities of the Korean war. However, on Sunday evening, the US president said he was “not happy” with US participation “based on my very good relationship with Kim Jong-un”. He added that they were costly and “send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile, to a country that, as long as Donald J Trump has been president, has been unthreatening and respectful”. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/23/fide.text: Menü Kereső Romanowskit megnevezve reagált a Fidesz az Alapjogokért Központnál tartott házkutatásra Belföld Pupli Anna Sára Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Szerda délután a Fidesz is reagált az Alapjogokért Központ háttércégénél hűtlen kezelés miatt tartott házkutatásra . A gyanú szerint a Fidesz-közeli elemző központ havi több mint bruttó 3,5 millió forintért foglalkoztattak egy volt külföldi tisztségviselőt, aki mindeközben alig végzett tényleges munkát a központnál, és aki jelenleg is nemzetközi körözés alatt áll. A párt újkommunista önkényről és politikai irányítás alá rendelt nyomozó irodáról ír közleményében – szerintük az eljárásnak nincs jogi alapja és csak idő kérdése volt, hogy a hatóságok „mikor támadják meg a jobboldal következő szellemi központját.” Ami az igazán érdekes a Fidesz reakciójában, hogy tényként kezelik, hogy az Orbán-kormány idején menedékjogot kapott volt lengyel igazságügyi miniszterhelyettesről, Marcin Romanowskiról van szó – pedig a rendőrség közleményében nem nevezte meg a külföldi férfit. „A rajtaütés ürügyeként felhozott lengyel politikai menekült ügye nem valósít meg semmilyen bűncselekményt. Marcin Romanowski a Tisza Párthoz hasonlóan Lengyelországban önkényt építő Tusk-kormány politikai üldözése elől menekült Magyarországra. A nemzeti kormány – folytatva elődeink hagyományát – a Lengyelországból érkező politikai menekülteknek menedéket nyújtott. A jobboldal tudásukat és tapasztalatukat felhasználta, tisztességes munkájukért tisztességes bért kaptak” – olvasható a Fidesz közleményében. Az egyébként még nyár elején derült ki, hogy Romanowski 17,5 millió forintot keresett az Alapjogokért Központnál. A hazájában korrupcióval gyanúsított volt miniszterhelyettes a Magyar-Lengyel Szabadság Intézetet vezette, amit direkt az ő kedvéért hozott létre a fideszes agytröszt. A Tisza-kormány aztán júliusban visszavonta Romanowski, illetve a volt lengyel igazságügyi miniszter Zbigniew Ziobro és felesége menekültstátuszát. A szerdai házkutatásra maga a Szánthó Miklós-féle Alapjogokért Központ is reagált. Azt írták, együttműködnek a hatóságokkal. Állításuk szerint megalakulásuk óta a jogszabályok betartásával végzik tevékenységüket, „ez így történt külföldi kutatóinkkal való együttműködés során is”. https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/ente.text: This week, the 51st Polish Feature Film Festival started with a screening of Wild Wild East. The film festival, which is called the Cannes of Polish cinema, attracts legends, aspiring directors, cinematographers, and cinephiles.You may think that at Cannes, movie tickets disappear in minutes â try booking a ticket at the Polish Film Festival. Such is the love for cinema among people.From the legendary filmmaker Andrzej Wajda's way of seeing the world to the current crop of cinematographers like Adam Pitkiewicz, the visual beauty of Polish cinema is unparalleled.As the film festival's artistic director Joanna ÅapiÅska puts it, âMasters are giving the torch to the next ones.âIn an interview, she spoke to us about the 51st edition and the beauty of films.'The 51st PIFF is diverse in terms of style, but of course in terms of subject as well, and generations.'From Hollywood's great filmmakers to Indian Bollywood films and independent films, Polish cinematographers are the ones everyone wants to work with.How difficult is it to curate a film festival like the Polish Film Festival, which is so prestigious and so important for the Polish industry?She says, âOn one hand, it is difficult because itâs a huge responsibility. When you see the festival, you probably noticed how huge an impact we can have on a film. Thatâs why, for some films, itâs really itâs all about being here.When they plan their promotion strategy, when they plan the release strategy for the film, they always hope that they can count Gdynia, our festival, in. And if we donât invite them, then sometimes we realise that we make the life of the film definitely shorter. So, of course, looking from this side, this is a huge responsibility.On the other side, I have to tell you that this is a good moment for Polish cinema - this year. We have 50â60 feature-length films submitted to the festival, and this is the proper number to choose from. This way, I can really build a strong, interesting programme, proving that Polish cinema is diverse, that it goes in different directions.Itâs diverse in terms of style, but of course in terms of subject as well, and generations.And this year really proves it because we have many first-time directors. On the other hand, we have all these names like Pawlikowski, Komasa, SmoczyÅska, SobociÅski, Å»ohorski, who is coming after many years with a new film."So this is a perfect balance of youth and tradition, the more experienced cinema.âPolish film industry calls PIFF the âPolish CannesâThe festival holds a lot of importance for newcomers, filmmakers, and people from the industry. Joanna shares,âFor the film industry, they even call it the Polish Cannes. And actually, there is something in it because, as we call it, everybody is here. Everybody comes to Gdynia.Not only to watch the films, but also to discuss where the film industry is. Thatâs why we have a huge segment of industry-oriented events, like the Gdynia Industry programme, which is really huge. It is diverse itself.Some people even say that this is like a separate festival, but this is, again, a little bit like Cannes. So itâs not like a market but there are so many discussions lined up.âShe continues, âeach of them wants to have space here. Each of them wants to discuss their particular problems. Sometimes, of course, they share the problems; sometimes they are totally separate. And still, we try to make them meet each other here and talk.But my thinking since the beginning is that we shouldnât do a promotional event. It should be a serious talk, which really takes us forward.âTalking about what they discuss, she adds, âAll the fears of our industry, starting with the problems with film financing. Youâll probably find similarities with India.In Poland, the system used to be quite secure like babysitting, because we have the Polish Film Institute. At some point, it was enough to submit your project there and the Institute â which is quite well financed because it is a tax-financed institution â would support it.So if you had a good project, there was always a huge chance that you were going to be given money. And then getting the rest wasnât that difficult.Now itâs difficult. So even if you are given the first part of the money by the Polish Film Institute, it doesnât mean that youâre going to close the financing. This is a serious problem.So, of course, this is a subject we discuss here.âShe continues, âWe talk about tax incentives here, not Polish ones this year, but looking at the countries around us and how we can use them.Because even if you look at the programme of the main competition, you notice immediately how many films have been made as co-productions with other countries.So co-producing films is another way to close the financing for cinema. We should also look around. We should discuss where to go and what the experiences are.âThey also talk about script development â how to improve it, at which stage to change it, which way to make the script stronger so that the film is stronger at the end.Then PIFF concentrates very much on young people starting their path in the film industry.Joanna shares, âFor them, I created, four years ago, a one-day-long programme called Gdynia Campus. Of course, you immediately hear âBerlinale Talents Campus.ââShe adds, âYes, so this is our Gdynia Campus. We invite film students from all film schools and film departments in Poland.And we do even more because we invite them beforehand. We have leaders from each school, and they are the ones who create the programme and choose the subjects they want to talk about.This is a really close collaboration. They are getting better and better every year, and the programme they build is very advanced and very precise.For example, this year itâs very practical. They want to talk about the second assistant director, for example.âItâs not only about the films you are watching, but also about this wider portrait which you get from watching them.Joanna has been a jury member of the Kolkata Film Festival and a film festival in Bengaluru. Talking about her experience, she shares, âIndian cinema is very diverse. I like being on the jury because this is the time when you can concentrate on a set of films somebody chose for you.And sometimes itâs not only about the films you are watching, but also about this wider portrait which you get from watching them.And always, you are given something extra. You are given the possibility to know other people and to talk to them on a very deep level about cinema, not only, of course, the films you are watching.I remember that from Kolkata â when we were watching our films from the competition, but then there was a huge presentation of Polish classics. So some of us were just running towards these films, and that was the start of the conversation about which cinema we love, which films we love.And, you know, we kept talking for hours, and that was great. This is what you also expect from that.And this year, I have to tell you that Iâm very happy because my jury members here at the festival approached me and said, âYou put us together really nicely. You just, I donât know how, but guessed our energy.âAnd they really spend time together talking about cinema, walking to the beach and still being this group of cinema lovers.Thatâs what I like about being on a jury.âGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq78.text: Figure caption, Watch: BBC breaks down body cam video of ICE shooting in New York By Ana Faguy Â and Â Kayla Epstein ,Â Reporting from New York court Published 9 October 2026 Updated 3 hours ago US immigration officials have defended officers who shot and wounded a man in his car in New York on Thursday while his five-year-old son was in the back seat. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) chief Markwayne Mullin said officers opened fire while trying to arrest a man with a criminal history. "We weren't aware the child was in the car," Mullin said, arguing that it was the man, Oscar Belgal, who had put his child in danger. Belgal is being held at a detention facility. His lawyers appeared at a hearing on his behalf on Friday. "The first thing he asked me, is whether his son is OK," his attorney Harold Solis said outside court. A handful of friends and family members, including a cousin and an aunt, attended the hearing but did not speak to the press. Another of his lawyers, Paige Austin, told the judge at the hearing that Belgal "still has a bullet in his body" and had been taken to the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn after being discharged from hospital. Austin said he had only been able to make a brief phone call within the hour prior to the hearing. The BBC has not been able to confirm his medical condition, but contacted DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The shooting happened in the residential neighbourhood of Marble Hill. Marcos Charles, a top ICE official, said the agency's officers used their vehicles to try and stop Belgal in his car but that he resisted orders to get out and instead accelerated, smashing into two ICE vehicles. Charles said Belgal then "weaponised his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate going towards other officers", adding: "Our officers, using their training, and believing that their life and the life of their partners in the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons." The number of officers who fired their weapons is being investigated. Charles said Belgal "was struck by one of the bullets or fragments superficially in the neck". New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who called what happened "unconscionable and incredibly serious", said ICE agents surrounded Belgal's car before opening fire. "They wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces. There is no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents," Mamdani said. He confirmed the child was unharmed. Mullin said the officers identified themselves and were wearing body-worn cameras that were turned on during the incident. Video of the shooting, including body camera footage, has not been made public but unverified videos on social media appear to align with Mamdani's comments. Body-worn camera footage released by the New York Police Department (NYPD) on Friday shows its officers arriving on scene and attempting to help Belgal after he has been shot. One ICE officer appears to be wearing a neon construction vest and carrying a large gun. The NYPD officers then call for an ambulance and put him in a police car to take him to hospital. They are later seen pulling Belgal from the vehicle and carrying him into the hospital. Figure caption, Watch: Outrage after person shot by ICE in New York Mamdani said on Thursday that he had spoken to US President Donald Trump and Mullin for two hours but failed to negotiate Belgal's release. Mamdani said he would ask Trump, who has not yet commented publicly on the shooting, to end ICE enforcement actions in New York. Mullin has said he will not pause enforcement. The DHS said Belgal, 28, was from the Dominican Republic and had "a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny and multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs and weapons possession". Belgal was arrested by police officers in New York in December 2023 and released "a few days later", according to the DHS. New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said there was also still a pending case against Belgal for criminal sale of a controlled substance in 2025. DHS has also alleged Belgal was associated with the Trinitarios, described by the US justice department as a transnational criminal group. Mullin said the DHS believed Belgal "has either indirect or direct knowledge" of a US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer shooting, "and that's why he became a target". Mamdani is not the only New York official to have criticised the incident. Governor Kathy Hochul said federal officials needed to provide answers quickly about what happened. "New Yorkers have witnessed far too many acts of violence by a rogue federal agency and untrained agents that operate with impunity," Hochul said, adding that she had spoken to Mullin and Trump as well. There have been several high-profile shootings involving ICE officers this year, including one that caused the death of Renee Good in Minneapolis in January.
